clue.text: When ill, Dick and Bess might take to these

definitions.text: When ill, Dick and Bess might take to these

indicators.note: something ill is out of sorts, so the names that follow are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple named Dick and Bess, feeling poorly, retire to where invalids lie.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the two names, made ill (jumbled), give exactly SICKBEDS, which is where the ill take to.
explanation.definitionFit: Beds occupied by patients during illness are where sufferers are said to take to when unwell.

clue.text: Deep pink and pale yellow fruit

parts.note: straw is a pale yellow colour
a berry is a small fruit

explanation.surface: A description of a fruit's colouring, pink and pale yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a list of colours for a fruit; the first colour is in fact the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Strawberry names a reddish-pink colour as well as the fruit.

clue.text: Perhaps Brown's not so very dull!

parts.note: brown is an example of a colour, signalled by perhaps
less means not so much

explanation.surface: A jibe that Gordon Brown, the prime minister when this appeared, is not so very boring after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Colourless figuratively means lacking interest or character, which is what dull means.

clue.text: Held and beat rebellious daughter

indicators.note: a rebellious thing refuses its usual order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent restrained and struck an unruly daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Bated survives mainly in 'with bated breath', meaning breath held back.
explanation.definitionFit: Bated means restrained or held in, as in breath held in suspense.

clue.text: Doctor, vicar, don, dame and politician

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters that follow are altered in order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A list of establishment figures: a medic, a cleric, an academic, a dame and an MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the first person in the list, but it is the verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: David Cameron was then leader of the Conservative Party and later prime minister, so an example of a politician.

clue.text: School's ideology causing split

parts.note: SCH is a standard abbreviation for school
an ism is any doctrine or ideology

explanation.surface: A school's doctrine has caused its members to divide.
explanation.definitionFit: A schism is a division or rupture within a group, typically a church, so it is a synonym of split.

clue.text: Type of community not restricted to Fair Isle

definitions.text: Type of community not restricted to Fair Isle

parts.note: surface reading: a tightly bonded group of people
setter's reading: Fair Isle is a style of patterned knitwear, and a tight stitch is not unique to it; also a remote Shetland island where the community is close

explanation.walkthrough: Fair Isle is both a tiny Shetland island and a famous pattern of knitted sweaters, so the phrase plays on tight knitting and tight communities.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-knit community is one whose members are bound by strong ties, like tightly interlocked stitches.

clue.text: I proposed to be in the same place as before

definitions.text: in the same place as before

parts.note: taken as written
to bid is to offer or propose

explanation.surface: Someone says they offered to stay where they were previously.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibid, short for Latin ibidem, is used in references to cite the same source just cited.

clue.text: Cooked meat for tea

indicators.note: cooking transforms raw ingredients, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Meat is prepared for the evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea' suggests the British evening meal, but it is the South American herbal drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Mate is a South American infusion brewed from yerba leaves, a kind of herbal drink.

clue.text: I travel abroad with English kinsman

indicators.note: going abroad scatters things far from their usual place, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone announces they are going overseas with an English cousin.
explanation.definitionFit: A relative is a family member, which is what a kinsman is.

clue.text: In favour of international currency

parts.note: to be for something is to favour it
INT is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: Someone backs a single global currency.
explanation.walkthrough: The forint is the currency of Hungary.
explanation.definitionFit: The forint is the monetary unit of Hungary, so it is an example of a currency.

clue.text: Dignitary meets nonconformist ranter and old adventurer

parts.note: a knight holds an honour, a dignitary

indicators.note: a nonconformist breaks the usual pattern, so the next word's letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grandee encounters a dissenting preacher and a veteran explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nonconformist ranter' suggests a Methodist preacher (Primitive Methodists were nicknamed Ranters), but nonconformist only shuffles the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight-errant was a medieval knight wandering in search of chivalrous adventures.

clue.text: Battle injury

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the 1890 massacre of Lakota people by US troops in South Dakota
second meaning: literally a hurt joint in the leg

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a single phrase, a wound from combat, but the two words are separate meanings: a famous engagement and, read literally, a damaged leg joint.
explanation.definitionFit: Wounded Knee is the name of an 1890 armed clash in South Dakota, and literally describes a hurt leg joint.

clue.text: I'm in a tangle of rope and nets, being a fisherman

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
a tangle is a muddled mass, so the letters of the following words are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone caught up in ropes and nets explains they fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Simon Peter was the apostle who was a fisherman on the Sea of Galilee.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle Simon Peter fished for a living before following Jesus, so he is an example of a fisherman.

clue.text: Things to lie on, made of fabric and hair

parts.note: a mat is a piece of woven material
tresses are long locks of hair

explanation.surface: A description of bedding stuffed with cloth and horsehair.
explanation.definitionFit: Mattresses are the padded bases of beds on which people sleep.

clue.text: Chapter in tale about success

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the word tale is read backwards
in places the chapter inside the other word

parts.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for chapter

explanation.surface: A chapter in a story concerns a triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat means brilliant success or acclaim, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Plant found above a Spanish town

parts.note: tarragon is an aromatic herb
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plant has been discovered growing over a town in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, one piece above another simply comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarragona is a port city in Catalonia, so an example of a Spanish town.

clue.text: Tearing about North America and a country in South America

indicators.note: something thrown about lands in a jumble, so the first word's letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
NA is the abbreviation for North America

explanation.surface: Someone rushes around the northern continent and then a southern nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tearing' looks like a verb of rushing, but it is simply the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a nation occupying much of the southern part of that continent.

clue.text: Scripture's very important and enjoying a revival

parts.note: RE is religious education, the school subject, here with its 's
something urgent is pressing and vital

explanation.surface: Bible study is vital and seeing a renewed popularity.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (religious education) is the British school subject once called scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Resurgent describes something rising again after a decline, which is enjoying a revival.

clue.text: Try to persuade people to consume right kind of fish

indicators.note: to consume is to take something inside, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: to tout is to solicit customers persistently
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone urges people to eat the proper sort of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Trout is a freshwater game fish of the salmon family, so it is one sort of fish.

clue.text: French love to strut about, showing vanity perhaps

parts.note: amour is the French word for love
a strut is a supporting prop
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A Frenchman loves to swagger around, which shows conceit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strut' suggests swaggering, but here it is the noun, a support.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour propre is self-esteem, and vanity is an excessive example of it, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Repeat some serene words

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken

parts.note: the letters run across the boundary of the two words

explanation.surface: Say a few calm words again.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew something such as a vow is to repeat it or make it again.

clue.text: A bird mating

parts.note: taken as written
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A bird in the breeding season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At it' is informal British slang for having sex.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom at it is colloquial for engaged in sexual activity, i.e. copulating.

clue.text: A hundred soldiers in Israeli city

parts.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
RE stands for Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A company of a hundred troops is stationed in a city in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Acre is an ancient port in northern Israel, so an example of a city there.

clue.text: Heartlessly try to acquire company with support of rich chap

indicators.note: without its heart a word loses its middle, leaving only its ends

parts.note: the outer letters of try
CO is the abbreviation for company
to rest on something is to be supported by it

explanation.surface: A ruthless attempt to take over a firm with a wealthy backer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tycoon is a wealthy and powerful businessman, so a rich man.

clue.text: Accountant ultimately manages restructuring for industrialists

indicators.note: restructuring rebuilds something in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of accountant
taken as written

explanation.surface: An accountant eventually takes charge of reorganising things for business bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnates are wealthy, influential business leaders, so industrialists are examples.

clue.text: Parent can become a bore

indicators.note: becoming something else implies changing form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mother or father may turn into a tedious person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' suggests a tiresome person, but here it is a tool that bores holes; a trepan is a surgical drill for the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: A trepan is a cylindrical saw or drill used for boring holes, particularly in surgery or mining.

clue.text: Officials set out charges

indicators.note: laid out, the first word's letters are spread and reordered

parts.note: taken as written
wards are people in one's charge

explanation.surface: Authorities lay out the fees to be paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' suggests fees, but here it means people in someone's care.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewards are people who supervise events or manage affairs, a kind of official.
